convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 indicators (iMA with MODE_EMA and MODE_LWMA). Simple entry/exit rules based on MA crossovers. Fixed or percentage-based position sizing with optional loss-based reduction. Standard Trade library used only for order execution, not custom logic.

derived_values.name: ema1 - EMA value at bar [1] (previous completed bar)
ema2 - EMA value at bar [2] (two bars back)
lwma1 - LWMA value at bar [1] (previous completed bar)
lwma2 - LWMA value at bar [2] (two bars back)

other_exits: Close buy position when LWMA[1] < EMA[1] (opposite of entry condition LWMA>EMA)
Close sell position when LWMA[1] > EMA[1] (opposite of entry condition LWMA<EMA)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If Lots>0: use fixed Lots value. If Lots==0: calculate as AccountFreeMargin * MaximumRisk / 1000.0, then normalize. If DecreaseFactor>0 and consecutive losses>1: reduce lot by (lot * losses / DecreaseFactor).

custom_logic_notes: Entry requires all three conditions simultaneously: LWMA above EMA on previous bar, LWMA rising (LWMA[1]>LWMA[2]), and EMA rising (EMA[1]>EMA[2]) for longs (reverse for shorts). Additionally, entry is blocked if the close signal for the same direction is also active (e.g. OpBuy && !ClBuy), preventing entry on weakening signals. Lot reduction logic counts consecutive losing deals backwards from trade history and reduces lot size proportionally. Deviation is set to Spread*3 for both entry and close operations.
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward dual-MA crossover system. Uses completed bar values (index 1 and 2 from CopyBuffer) not current bar, so bar-close basis is clean. No SL/TP on orders — exits are purely signal-based (LWMA crosses below EMA closes longs, LWMA crosses above EMA closes shorts). The lot normalization function accounts for min volume, volume step, and max volume — replicate this exactly. The DecreaseFactor lot reduction iterates deal history in reverse counting consecutive losses — must replicate this history scan. The entry guard (!ClBuy for longs, !ClSell for shorts) prevents opening when the close signal is already active, which is important to preserve. Trade deviation is dynamic at 3x current spread.
